title: Final: context and deadlock
sub: Hang the program, then fix it three ways
cards/0/task: Drive the WPF app into a deadlock.
cards/1/task: Fix it the right way: no ConfigureAwait, and stay in WPF.
cards/2/q: Which fix is a safety net rather than a cure?
cards/2/explain: The thread still blocks on .Result; the deadlock loop just never closes.
cards/3/q: Where do you need the captured context after await? Select all that apply.
cards/3/options/1: A Unity script moves a transform
cards/3/options/3: An ASP.NET Core controller reads the database
cards/3/explain: A library or a server doesn't need the UI thread.
cards/4/q: Which line can hang a WPF app?
cards/4/explain: .Result on the UI thread while SaveAsync awaits inside without ConfigureAwait(false).
cards/5/q: Why doesn't the same line hang an ASP.NET Core server?
cards/5/options/0: There's no context, so the pool runs the continuation; but the thread still sits idle
cards/5/explain: Instead of a deadlock you get thread-pool starvation under load.
cards/6/q: The wait cycle in a deadlock
cards/6/items/0: The UI thread waits for the task
cards/6/items/1: The task waits for its continuation
cards/6/items/2: The continuation waits for the UI thread
